subject: arcadeCabinet
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static synthwave-style arcade cabinet, using createBuilder and part geometry without needing joints since nothing moves. I'm sizing it realistically—around 1.8m tall, 0.66m wide, 0.8m deep—facing forward along +Z.

I'm working out the side-panel silhouette by extruding a 2D outline in the z-y plane: sketching the cabinet's profile from base to control deck, up through the recessed monitor slope, to the marquee top, making sure the points form a clean, non-intersecting counterclockwise loop.

For the body color I'm going with a dark navy-purple, and for side art I'm planning thin neon stripe boxes placed on the outer panel faces and rotated to run diagonally across the surface.

Still placing stripes and adding a sun disc...

Adding the coin door with slots and glowing buttons, then working out the back panel geometry to roughly match the tapering side profile with a slightly angled box rather than a precise slant.

Still placing control deck geometry...

Now I'm positioning the screen bezel on the sloped surface, calculating the tilt angle from the slope's direction vector so the top edge leans back slightly, then placing it centered with a small offset along the surface normal.

For the screen content itself, I'm setting up a local coordinate helper to place a synthwave scene inside the bezel—a glowing sun circle, horizon grid lines, and mountain silhouettes—using the same rotation and the slope's direction and normal vectors to position each flat element correctly.

Working out the geometry transforms...

Working out the local coordinate transforms so z-axis points outward from the slope, then building the screen's layered geometry starting with the bezel frame box positioned on that surface.

Now I'm designing the glass pane within the bezel, splitting it into six horizontal sky-gradient bands running from deep purple at top to pink-orange near the horizon, plus a dark floor strip and a sun circle whose lower half gets cut by overlapping gradient stripes to create a retro sunset effect.

Thinking through layering: floor should sit at a higher z than the sun to hide its bottom portion below the horizon line, and I'm adding thin colored stripes across the sun at a few y-positions to mimic the synthwave look. For mountains, I'm considering using angled cone shapes placed near the horizon edges to suggest distant peaks.

Still working out the mountain geometry...

Now I'm setting up the retro grid floor with horizontal glowing cyan lines spaced closer together as they approach the horizon, plus vertical lines converging toward the vanishing point to create the classic perspective grid effect.

Now I'm adding a glow pass across the screen, glass, and sky elements with high intensity. For the marquee, I'm building a panel box at the top with a dark purple base color, then adding a neon-style "NEON RACER" title rendered via an SVG texture on a plane, glowing to sell the arcade sign look.

Writing marquee texture SVG...

I'm trimming the marquee with glowing magenta and cyan neon tube rods along its edges, then moving down to the control panel deck -- adding a dark purple top plate and starting on the joystick assembly with a base disc, shaft cylinder, and red/magenta ball top.

Still figuring out joystick and button placements...

Adding the glowing front edge strip and the coin door assembly below it, with silver coin plates, dark slits, and red return buttons flanking the center.

Now I'm working on the side panels, setting their thickness and offset from the core, and picking a deep purple-blue base color. I'm also planning thin neon tube outlines swept along the cabinet's side silhouette edges to add glowing trim.

For the sweep, I'll close the outline into a polyline with rounded corners, give it a cyan glow, and inset it slightly from the true edge by scaling points toward a centroid so the glow sits inside the silhouette rather than right on it.

I'm skipping extra decorations like a coin door or screen text to keep things simple, maybe just adding stripes or chevrons to the lower side art, plus small leveler feet cylinders at the corners.

Rather than a separate base plinth, I decide a dark kick band box at the front bottom is simpler and avoids z-fighting with the core color. Now I'm thinking about rear details like a vent grid and power cable on the back door.

For the vent, I plan six slim slats angled to match the back panel's slight slope, and for the cable I consider a curved tube path from the unit down to the floor, but weigh whether to skip it since it's low risk either way.

Settling on the color palette with marquee coloration, side sun motif, and stripe accents. I decide to skip any floor underglow since no ground was requested, but add an LED chaser row of alternating colored spheres beneath the marquee, plus bezel corners, coin lights, side stripes, and decorative control panel arrows to round out the part count toward 150.

Setting up the builder helper functions...

I'm checking that core and side faces don't z-fight since adjacent surfaces meet without overlapping, and confirming the outline triangulates fine even with concavity. Now I'm starting a transform helper for screen placement.

Still writing screen helper...

Checking bezel dimensions against the slope geometry to confirm the top edge aligns with the outline point, then verifying bezel width stays within the core panel bounds before placing the marquee plane.

For the marquee itself, I'm designing an SVG texture with a dark purple gradient, sun circle, grid lines, and "TURBO NIGHTS" text in an italic Impact-style font with stroke outline, applied to a plane geometry with glow strength around 0.9. Then I'm positioning cyan neon edge tubes along the top and bottom of the marquee outline to match the frame coordinates.

Now I'm sketching out the control panel details: a joystick with a dark disc base, silver shaft, and red ball top, plus a row of colored button cylinders with dark rings, and placing them at calculated positions along the panel.

For the sun I'm simplifying to layered concentric discs instead of true half-cylinder gradients: a large yellow disc, an orange disc inset and shifted down, and a small pink disc further inset, giving a sunset gradient look with horizontal bars layered below in the dark side color.

Now I'm positioning tilted rainbow stripe boxes across the body, calculating their rotated extents so each stripe (pink, orange, yellow, cyan) stays within the body bounds, spaced evenly with a 30° tilt.

I'll give the two side edges different colors, magenta on the right and cyan on the left, for a bit of visual flair. Then I'll add the back vent and cable before finalizing the write.
